title: P300 dataset from Hoffmann et al 2008
description: A P300 brain-computer interface dataset comprising EEG recordings from 8 subjects (4 disabled, 4 able-bodied) performing a visual oddball task with image stimuli. The dataset includes 32-channel EEG data sampled at 2048 Hz from 4 sessions per subject, with 810 total trials (135 targets, 675 non-targets) classified using Fisher's linear discriminant analysis and Bayesian linear discriminant analysis. This derivative dataset demonstrates high classification accuracy (100%) and information transfer rates suitable for BCI applications in disabled populations.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Biosemi ActiveTwo system with 32 active electrodes at 2048 Hz sampling rate. Subjects performed a visual P300 oddball task counting silently when prescribed images were flashed among six possible stimuli (television, telephone, lamp, door, window, radio) presented with 400 ms inter-stimulus intervals. Each trial lasted 1 second with stimulus flash duration of 100 ms. Four sessions of 6 runs each were conducted per subject without feedback.
